title: job.hook_failed
description: The delivery of a hook declared in the graph exhausted its six attempts and gave up. It is an incident, not an outcome: the job does not change node, is not blocked and never learns this happened — a hook never takes part in the traversal. It exists because a hook has no registered subscriber: nobody is polling its queue, and without this event the reaction declared by whoever wrote the graph would fail silently. No parity in flowpilot — it is born with the transition hooks (t169).

hook_id.description: The id of the hook inside the graph document, as whoever wrote the graph named it. It is what the failed declaration is found by.

node_id.description: The node whose entry or block fired the hook. Without it, "which stage has a broken reaction?" can only be answered by reconstructing the traversal event by event.

url.description: The destination that did not answer. Copied from the delivery row, and not re-read from the graph: a new version may have changed the destination since, and the incident is about what was attempted.

last_error.description: What the sixth and last attempt returned — an HTTP status, a timeout or the message of the exception. It is what somebody debugging a mute integration looks for first.
